title: Thoracic range of motion
summary: Apply pure moments to thoracic spines with intact rib cage, or to single segments, and report total, regional and segmental rotation.
simulate: Build the specimen of the simulation: T1-T12 with intact rib cage; FSUs or 4-vertebra segments with rib heads/stumps but no rib cage; or a T2-sacrum spine without ribs.
Fix the caudal vertebra (T12, the lowest vertebra, or the sacrum); apply a pure moment to the cranial vertebra; leave the other 5 DOF free.
Preload only if listed: follower load along a path through the vertebral centres, or a fixed vertical axial force.
One-direction simulations: neutral to peak. "L+R" and "Flexion+extension": sum of both directions (full range).
Report every listed output (total, regional, segmental ROM, neutral zone) as one curve over the sweep.

outputs.label: Segmental ROM
outputs.definition: ROM = rotation of the upper vertebra relative to the lower at peak moment, loading branch (deg)

outputs.label: Total or regional ROM
outputs.definition: Total/regional ROM = rotation of the top vertebra of the span (T1, or T4/T8) relative to its bottom vertebra at peak moment (deg)

outputs.label: Neutral zone
outputs.definition: Neutral zone = rotation between loading and unloading branches at 0 Nm, both directions summed (deg)

notes: One direction (e.g. Flexion) and both directions summed (Flexion+extension, L+R) are separate tasks; moments differ (2, 5, 7.5, 8 Nm).
The rib cage roughly halves segmental ROM: compare rib-cage tasks with rib-cage models and single-segment tasks with FSU models.
Most Ulm values (Wilke 2025, Liebsch) are medians on overlapping donors; Busscher 2009 mid-segments keep 3 cm rib stumps.
agent_prompt: You have a finite element model of the human thoracic spine (ligamentous, no muscles). Run the 23 simulations in `simulations`. 'with rib cage' = T1-T12 with ribs, costal cartilage, sternum and costovertebral joints; 'without rib cage' = FSUs with rib heads or 4-vertebra segments with 3 cm rib stumps (report the middle segment); the 8/6 Nm test uses a T2-sacrum spine without ribs. Fix the caudal vertebra, apply the pure moment to the cranial one in the simulation's direction with the listed preload (0 = none), and sweep the moment (or the follower load where the moment is fixed). Report in degrees: rom_total = rotation of the region end vertebrae (T1 vs T12, or e.g. T4 vs T8), rom_segmental = upper vs lower vertebra at each level, nz = neutral zone (both directions; null if your model is elastic). One-direction: neutral to peak; full range (flexion+extension, L+R): both directions summed. Run each simulation once, sweeping the input in `sweep` over all its listed values (start from the unloaded state; a denser curve is fine), and record every listed output. Return one JSON object following answer_format: per simulation id, one curve [[x, y], ...] per output (x = the sweep input; it is read by linear interpolation and listed x values outside your curve fail), or one number where there is no sweep or the output is marked scalar; null where your model cannot run it. Do not tune the model to the reference values.
